newsitem.title: NORWAY: Smedvig, Statoil buy Shell ship.
newsitem.headline: Smedvig, Statoil buy Shell ship.

text.p: Norwegian offshore group Smedvig ASA said on Friday it had bought together with Den norske stats oljeselskap ASA the former storage vessel from the UK central North Sea Fulmar oilfield for about $5 million from operator Shell UK.
The vessel will be marketed as a floating production unit for projects in the Far East and West Africa, a statement from Smedvig said.

Smedvig and Statoil will establish a jointly-owned shipping company responsible for marketing and converting the vessel. This new company will award a management contract for marketing and operations to Smedvig.

The Fulmar storage vessel, built in 1968 as a very large crude carrier (VLCC), has been converted and upgraded several times. It is currently moored outside Stavanger on the west coast of Norway, where it will remain while preparations are made for its removal at the end of February, 1997, Smedvig said.
The company said the acquisition was in line with its commitment to continued expansion in the mobile production sector.
